title: Man and woman charged after baby boy found dead in Adelaide motel
text:
A man and a woman have been charged after a baby boy was found dead in a motel.

Benjamin Nicholas Houghton, 40, and Yue Ning Lieu, 42, are in custody after police discovered the child during a welfare check at a Glen Osmond motel in Adelaide’s south on Saturday.

“The infant had been deceased for a period of time,” South Australia police said in a statement on Tuesday.

A post-mortem confirmed the boy was aged between six and seven months old, police said.

The man and woman had been living at the Tollgate Motel since they arrived in SA at the start of the year, police said.

Houghton and Lieu have been charged with criminal neglect and destroy human remains to pervert the course of justice.

Their matters appeared in Adelaide magistrates court on Monday.

They did not apply for bail and were remanded in custody until 3 May 2027.

SA police’s eastern district detectives conducted the initial investigation.

“However, due to the nature and complexity of the incident and the resources required, Major Crime Investigation Branch have taken over the investigation,” a police statement said.

“Police are seeking assistance from anyone who has stayed at the Tollgate Motel, and specifically anyone who has information about the occupants of room four to contact Crime Stoppers.”

title: Bacon, eggs and Bowie: how year 12 English students tackled ‘human strength and vulnerability’ in HSC paper
text:
“How does the composer of your prescribed text offer you opportunities to examine assumptions about human strength and vulnerability?”

This was the bamboozling English question tens of thousands of year 12 students sat down to answer on the first day of their final school exams.

Kayden Tran, 18, had a “really great breakfast” of rice, bacon and eggs – but was it enough to get through an essay exploring tenacity and sensitivity in the writings of Tim Winton, George Orwell or Malala Yousafza?

“This morning, I felt extremely stressed and I kind of gave up hope,” the student of Canley Vale high school in Sydney’s west told the Guardian.

“But after doing the exam, I feel perfectly fine, I feel content, like I did the best I possibly could,” he said after the HSC English 1 paper on Tuesday.

Mary Alnimry listened to the song Heroes by the late David Bowie to prepare.

“I discovered that song through an assessment for year 10 and, every time, before every English exam, I listen to that song and it just reminds me of English,” she said.

The pair was among about 200 Canley Vale students to sit the test, just one cohort in the roughly 75,000 students across New South Wales working to wrap up their high school careers.

“You just have to go in and believe that you know the content,” Alnimry, 17, said. “That’s how I felt in the morning. And then after the exam, obviously it’s really rewarding. I completed everything, but there’s always that curiosity lingering.

“I think that it was pretty fair, there was nothing out of the ordinary.”

On Reddit, other year 12 students weren’t as confident.

“Honestly I think that’ll kick most people in the ass, the fact the question had so much to unpack I personally found it hard to address it all, I focused on vulnerability and strength and sprinkled a bit of assumptions,” one student with the handle bberson wrote on Tuesday afternoon.

Another, djungleskog41, was concerned they skipped over parts of the question: “I did Orwell too and tbh I didn’t address the question at all. I only focused on how like human vulnerability and weakness forces us to submit into the regime and rebelling is a sign of human strength blah blah blah but i barely mentioned my assumption so im rlly upset about that lol.”

Alana Miller, an English teacher at Canley Vale high school, has shepherded 17 years of year 12 students through the exams. She said the nerves don’t stop with students, and she too woke up this morning with the year 12s on her mind.

“We care so much about the students, we spend so much time,” she said. “We want them to do well, we want them to feel particularly that these exams are something they could achieve in.”

Fantasy books have been a growing hit at Canley Vale high alongside Japanese manga. Miller said she’s spent the past year trying to meet students where they are to help engage the next generation of readers.

“I think the best way is to … talk to them about books, shows, films that they might see,” Miller said

title: HIV screening to be intensified in Malappuram
text:
HIV testing in the district will be intensified as part of the National AIDS Control Programme. The decision was taken at a review meeting held here on Tuesday (October 13) to assess the Mobilisation of AIDS Safety (MAS) activities in the district.

The meeting discussed conducting tests in identified hotspots and strengthening HIV testing services at private hospitals.

M. Peeyush Namboothiripad, Additional Director of the Health department and project director of the Kerala State AIDS Control Society, presided over the meeting. Disha cluster programme manager S. Sunil Kumar welcomed the participants.

District AIDS control officer L. Sheena Lal, reproductive and child health (RCH) officer-in-charge K.M. Nuna Marja, deputy district medical officer C. Shubin, and district panchayat finance officer Mohammed Basheer spoke.

Officials from different departments and project coordinators working under the AIDS control society attended.

title: College student drowns in lake while swimming with friends
text:
A 20-year-old college student drowned in Hesaraghatta Lake after he went swimming with his friends instead of attending college, the police said. The deceased, Harsha, was the son of Vishwanath and Bhavya, residents of Kamakshipalya.

According to reports, Harsha had completed the Ganesh puja at home on Monday and had told his mother that a Ganesha idol had been installed at his college. He then left home, but instead of going to college, he went to Hesaraghatta Lake with his friends.

While swimming, Harsha reportedly entered deeper waters and drowned after struggling to swim.

On receiving information about the incident, Soladevanahalli police and Fire and Emergency Services personnel rushed to the spot and launched a search operation.

With the assistance of local diving expert Eshwar Malpe, the team recovered Harsha’s body from the lake.

The body was shifted to the Victoria Hospital mortuary for a post-mortem examination. The Soladevanahalli police have registered a case and have initiated further investigation.

The incident has left Harsha’s family devastated.

title: Response to petitions on illegal detention, clampdown is ready, but needs fine-tuning: Centre
text:
The Union government informed the Supreme Court on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) that its response to petitions alleging illegal detentions, shutdown of public and rail transport, including Metro service, in Delhi on October 10 is “ready” but needs more fine-tuning.

A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant extended the time for the government to file the reply affidavit by Thursday (October 15).

Anti-CEC protests LIVE updates

Multiple petitions, including ones seeking contempt proceedings, were adjourned to October 15, 2026 as one of the judges on the Bench was unwell. The Bench rose for the day shortly thereafter.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, for the Centre, said he had gone through the prepared affidavit. It was final, but he wanted to make it “more comprehensive”.

On the petitioners’ request, the Court asked him to share the affidavit, if possible, by October 14, 2026, a day before the hearing so that the lawyers on the petitioners were suitably well-versed with the contents of the affidavit and the hearing would be a meaningful one on Thursday.

The Court also agreed to urgently hear fresh petitions seeking independent probe and contempt proceedings against authorities on the continued police action against journalists, especially women media professionals, covering the anti-CEC/SIR protests despite an apex court order on October 11.

Chief Justice Kant asked the petitioners to cure defects, after which the pleas would also be put up for a comprehensive hearing on Thursday (October 15, 2026). The court asked for a senior police officer to be present during the next hearing, when allegations of assault on women are raised in the courtroom.

Members of the Supreme Court Bar Association and Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association, of which petitions were adjourned on October 13, gathered at the Supreme Court lawns to express solidarity with advocates who were assaulted and detained by the police during the October 10 and October 11 protests.

A separate petition was orally mentioned by senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia about the “sad” incident which happened in the Supreme Court on October 12, 2026. Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and other Opposition leaders had come to the Supreme Court Registry after filing a petition seeking a probe into the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and allegations of arbitrary functioning and misconduct against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Mr. Gandhi’s arrival had drawn a crowd of lawyers around the Registry block within the Supreme Court premises, and the participants of his ‘March for Democracy’ converged in large numbers at the outer gates of the court.

Mr. Bhatia said the petition filed by advocates has sought initiation of criminal contempt against Mr. Gandhi and other Opposition leaders for obstructing justice along with a ban on political demonstrations inside court premises, a “neutral framework” to regulate protests near courts, and safeguards agai

title: BJP women MPs seek President’s intervention to suspend Congress MP from Lok Sabha
text:
Women MPs from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) met President Droupadi Murmu and sought her intervention in suspending Congress MP and former Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) academic Angomcha Bimol Akoijam, from the Lok Sabha.

The JNU administration dismissed Mr. Akoijam on October 9, 2026, after an internal enquiry found him guilty of sexual harassment and inappropriate conduct following complaints from female students. He was a Professor at the university’s Centre for the Study of Social Systems in the School of Social Sciences.

BJP Mahila Morcha president Roop Kumari Choudhary told reporters after the meeting that the delegation, led by party MP D. Purandeswari, also urged the President to ensure the safety of those who had reported the alleged harassment.

BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj was among the delegation members.

The meeting followed a protest by the BJP Mahila Morcha on Monday (October 12, 2026), when its members took out a march and staged a demonstration outside the Congress headquarters in Delhi, demanding the party expel Mr. Akoijam. He represents the Inner Manipur constituency in the Lok Sabha.

title: Air show: ‘Q’ entry for gold card holders
text:
Gold card holders can watch the Dasara Air Show at Bannimantap grounds in Mysuru on October 18 and 19 through the designated ‘Q’ enclosure, according to the district administration.

A press release issued by the Dasara Special Officer said that tourists and others who have purchased gold cards must enter the venue through the designated access point and produce a valid card.

Entry will be permitted between 9 a.m. and 10.30 a.m. on both days. Only one person will be allowed entry per gold card, the release said.

title: Report sought on police action against SIR protest in Bengaluru, there will be no double standards: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar
text:
Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said he had taken note of the police action against protesters and members of the media on Monday (October 12, 2026), and had sought a full report on the circumstances that led to it. “If there has been any unnecessary use of force or excess, accountability will follow,” he said.

This comes a day after the Bengaluru police detained over 100 persons for attempting to march to the office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), Karnataka, to protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The police also manhandled journalists and photographers, apart from protesters, on a day when Mr. Shivakumar was participating in a protest rally against SIR in New Delhi, drawing widespread criticism.

“The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy. We cannot demand that right for ourselves in Delhi and deny it to others in Bengaluru. Karnataka must hold itself to the democratic standards that we expect from the rest of the country. There will be no double standards,” the Chief Minister said in a statement issued on Tuesday (October 13, 2026).

“Let me be clear: disagreement with the Election Commission, disagreement with my government or disagreement with me personally does not diminish anyone’s right to peacefully express it,” he added.

‘Do not disrupt peaceful protest’

Meanwhile, Home Minister Priyank Kharge said he had issued instructions to the police to ensure that no peaceful demonstration is disrupted.

“The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy. It must be respected, protected and never suppressed. I have issued instructions to the police to ensure that no peaceful demonstration is disrupted,” Mr. Kharge wrote on X on Tuesday.

“Our responsibility is not merely to maintain law and order, but to create an environment where every citizen can express dissent freely, peacefully and without fear. In a democracy, peaceful dissent is not a threat to law and order. It is a right that law and order must protect,” he added.

title: Three men from Rajasthan arrested for theft of dry fruits worth ₹6.11 lakh in Bengaluru
text:
The V.V. Puram police have arrested three men from Rajasthan for allegedly breaking into a dry fruits shop in New Taragupet and stealing dry fruits worth lakhs of rupees and some cash.

The arrested have been identified as Kailash, 23, from Beawar district; Dileep, 32, from Jodhpur district; and Om Prakash, 26, from Pali district in Rajasthan, Bengaluru Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh said at a press conference.

The police have recovered dry fruits worth ₹6.11 lakh and have seized the car allegedly used to commit the offence. Efforts are under way to trace and arrest another accused who is absconding.

According to the complaint lodged by the shop owner with the V.V. Puram police on September 24, unidentified persons broke open the shutter lock of the shop during the night of September 23 and decamped with 250 kg of almonds, 10 kg of pistachios, 10 kg of cashew nuts, 10 kg of another variety of almonds, and ₹8,000 in cash kept in a drawer.

Following the complaint, the police registered a theft case and launched an investigation, which led to the arrest of the three accused.

Further investigation is under way.

title: Farmers stop youth from jumping from signpost during protest
text:
Farmers stopped a young man who was trying to jump to the ground from the top of a signpost bar during the protest by sugarcane farmers at Hattargi village in Belagavi district on Tuesday (October 13).

Laxmikant Mardi, 25, of Tukkanatti village, had climbed the pole halfway when someone noticed him and pulled him down.

He told the crowd that he was upset at the Union government for failing to fulfil farmers’ demands. “I decided to end my life to bring attention to the cause of farmers. I was greatly worried about the plight of farmers who are not getting remunerative prices ,’’ he said.

Senior activists consoled him and asked him to continue peaceful protests till their demands were met.

title: Woman stranded in Kuwait repatriated, attends husband’s funeral in East Godavari
text:
A 35-year-old woman, Chintala Nagalakshmi, who was stranded in Kuwait, has been repatriated and reunited with her family in Munipalle village of Nidadavolu Mandal in East Godavari district on Tuesday to attend her husband’s last rites.

Ms. Nagalakshmi who works as a housemaid in Kuwait, through a video shared online, had appealed to the Andhra Pradesh State government for her repatriation. She had reportedly failed to convince her owner in Kuwait to let her leave for India on Monday. Her owner had reportedly demanded ₹3 lakh, citing the employment contract under which she was hired.

Ms. Nagalakshmi had sought to return to India after she received a communication about the death of her husband, Ch. Venkatesh, who had died of electrocution in Munipalle village on Monday. Meanwhile, his family members received his body after a postmortem was conducted at the Tanuku government hospital on Tuesday.

Responding to her online appeal, Minister for Tourism and Culture Kandula Durgesh alerted the concerned officials and the Andhra Pradesh Non-Resident Telugu Society in Kuwait to facilitate her repatriation.

In an official release on Tuesday, Mr. Durgesh said; “Ms. Nagalakshmi has arrived in India and reunited with her family on Tuesday. She also attend her husband’s last rites.”

title: Mysuru selected for pilot project to provide tap water to every household
text:
The decision to implement the ‘Clean water for every household’ (Drink Directly from Tap) initiative on a pilot basis in Mysuru city was taken at a meeting chaired by Urban Development Minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah here on Tuesday.

The initiative aims to supply clean drinking water directly to every household through taps. The meeting discussed the necessary measures to implement the pilot project in Mysuru within one year.

Several cities in Western countries have established systems to supply clean drinking water directly to households through taps. With the objective of ensuring convenient access to safe and clean drinking water for urban residents, the meeting deliberated on introducing a similar system in Karnataka.

The meeting discussed the technical requirements, feasibility and potential challenges involved in establishing a system that supplies clean drinking water directly to households through taps. Mysuru has been selected for the pilot implementation of this initiative in Karnataka.

M. G. Mathi Vathanan, retired Additional Chief Secretary of the Government of Odisha, attended the meeting and shared his experience in implementing the initiative in Odisha. He offered several suggestions regarding the project’s technical framework, feasibility and effective implementation.

The meeting deliberated on the comprehensive transformation of slum areas, technology-driven implementation, strengthening social infrastructure and sustainable livelihood models.

Discussions focused on strategies to improve the quality of life in urban settlements, enhance access to basic civic amenities, leverage technology for effective project planning and implementation, and strengthen community participation.

The meeting also explored opportunities to promote inclusive urban development and improve the living standards of urban residents through integrated social infrastructure and sustainable livelihood opportunities.

It was decided that, following the pilot implementation of the drinking water project in Mysuru, its outcomes, advantages and challenges would be comprehensively assessed before considering its expansion to other urban areas across the State.

The meeting was attended by B. B. Kaveri, Secretary to the Government, Urban Development Department; the Director of the Directorate of Municipal Administration (DMA); the Director of the Karnataka Urban Water Supply and Drainage Board (KUWSDB); and other senior officials.

title: Congress govt. implementing voter-roll revision exercise in Telangana, says Kishan
text:
Union Coal and Mines Minister G. Kishan Reddy on Tuesday defended the Election Commission of India’s ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, questioning whether it was wrong to remove the names of “deceased persons, illegal immigrants and other ineligible voters” from the rolls.

Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Mr. Reddy said the Congress government in Telangana was implementing the voter-roll revision exercise and that any mistakes found during the process should be corrected through proper channels.

“If there are errors, evidence must be presented. It is the responsibility of all stakeholders to identify and rectify them,” he said. He pointed out that the Congress party has Booth Level Agents (BLAs) at polling stations across the country and argued that they have adequate opportunities to flag and rectify instances where eligible voters may have been wrongly removed.

The BJP leader claimed that the revision exercise had identified nearly 2.8 crore deceased voters, while about 6.3 crore people had migrated from their original places of residence, and further alleged that around one crore voters were “registered in two places”, raising concerns about duplicate entries in electoral rolls.

He also accused Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of spreading misinformation by claiming that the voter-roll revision exercise was aimed at removing the names of poor people, Adivasis, Dalits and minorities. It is an attempt to create divisions based on caste, religion, language and economic status, he said.

He alleged that the Chief Minister and all Ministers are camping in the capital, instead of focusing on the challenges faced by the farmers due to water shortage and power cuts being faced by the industry and the public.

title: CPI(M) accuses Satheesan of kowtowing to RSS’ bid to subvert ED to ensnare Pinarayi in false cases
text:
Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] on Tuesday accused Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan of “slyly playing second fiddle” to the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh’s (RSS) national political agenda to weaken the secular opposition to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led Central government by subverting the Enforcement Directorate (ED) as a cat’s paw to foist false charges against top Left Democratic Front (LDF) leaders, including former Chief Minister and Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan in the CMRL-Exalogic pay-off case.

CPI(M) State secretary M.V. Govindan told a press conference that Mr. Satheesan’s statement that the government would not appeal the High Court single Bench order to register an FIR against Mr. Vijayan, his daughter T. Veena, and former Minister P.A. Mohamed Riyas, based on a legally dubious report filed by the ED, was the latest corroboration of Mr. Satheesan’s “enduring cosy deal and symbiotic association” with the Sangh Parivar.

Mr. Govindan pointed out that the UDF indicted Mr. Vijayan and his family in an anti-corruption case at the drop of a hat, “ignoring the Advocate General’s advice that the Enforcement Directorate (ED)’s demand seeking an immediate FIR against the CPI(M) leader without a preliminary inquiry was opaque and did not establish a cognisable offence.”

In contrast, Mr. Govindan said the non-BJP governments in Tamil Nadu and Punjab had shown the legal and political grit to protect their constitutionally guaranteed jurisdictional mandate over law-enforcement matters from the Centre’s extra-judicial interference by rejecting similar ED demands to ensnare anti-Sangh Parivar leaders in false cases.

“The All India Congress Committee (AICC) should state whether Mr. Satheesan’s dalliance with the RSS and its allied Central agencies had the national leadership’s imprimatur. The AICC should explain why Mr. Satheesan’s actions and statements in Kerala were at variance with the Congress’ national line against the BJP’s abuse of the ED and the CBI to settle political scores, weaken the secular opposition, and also arm-twist opposition politicians into throwing in their lot with the RSS,” he said.

Mr. Govindan noted that, for political expediency and possibly to curry favour with the BJP, the government overlooked the fact that the Vigilance court, the High Court and the Supreme Court had dismissed a plea (filed by Congress legislator Mathew Kuzhalnadan) to bring anti-corruption charges against Mr. Vijayan in the CMRL-Exalogic case.

Mr. Govindan said the UDF also wilfully discounted the ED’s attempt to indict Mr. Vijayan, which was based on statements extorted from two CMRL officials under “duress” and later legally recanted in affidavits, in haste to ensnare the CPI(M) leader in a false case.

title: SP reviews security in Tadipatri ahead of local body elections
text:
Anantapur Superintendent of Police (SP) P. Jagadeesh on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) reviewed security arrangements at the EVM distribution centre, counting centres and the nomination centre in Tadipatri, a reportedly sensitive town in the district, ahead of the local body elections.

He visited the hyper-sensitive areas of Nandalapadu, Om Shakti Nagar and Srinivasa Puram in Tadipatri and held a special meeting with the police officials of Tadipatri division.

At the Polytechnic College in the town, he inspected the proposed EVM distribution centre and vote counting centres and gave instructions to the officials on the security of election materials, routes for the movement of staff and security measures to be taken during counting.

Mr. Jagadeesh also inspected the Tadipatri Municipal Office, where the nomination filing process would be held, and discussed with the local officials the implementation of election rules during the receipt of nominations, the movement of candidates and their supporters, and precautionary measures to maintain law and order. He said security arrangements should be made at the nomination centre to prevent any tension.

Tadipatri Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) M. Chandrasekhar, circle inspectors of the division and others also took part in the inspection.

title: MEA reaffirms Ladakh is an integral part of India, says China’s denial cannot change facts
text:
China on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) strongly opposed India’s move to standardise names for 28 strategic locations and geographical features in Ladakh, reiterating its claim over the region.

China has never recognised the “so-called Union Territory of Ladakh”, which India “unilaterally and illegally established”, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said at a media briefing in Beijing.

Ms. Mao was responding to India’s Ministry of Home Affairs announcing standardised names for 28 locations and geographical features in Ladakh.

On October 2, India formally assigned standardised names to 28 strategic locations and geographical features in Ladakh, including key border friction points along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), such as Gogra and Hot Springs, on its official map.

Responding to media queries on comments made by the Chinese side regarding Ladakh, Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal reiterated that the Union Territory of Ladakh is an integral and inalienable part of India, adding that no amount of denial by China can change this fact.

The Ministry of External Affairs said the Ministry of Home Affairs’ press release was self-explanatory, noting that 28 places and geographical features in the Union Territory of Ladakh had been assigned standardised names on the official Survey of India map in consultation with the UT administration and local stakeholders. It added that the move aims to ensure accurate identification of these locations and improve public awareness.

title: Cop suspended for attacking SFI workers
text:
A civil police officer attached to the Armed Reserve (AR) camp here was suspended on Tuesday following a complaint that he assaulted SFI activists with a knuckleduster while under the influence of alcohol. The officer named Safad, a native of Chittilanchery, was suspended by the District Police Chief after the Town North Police reported that he had been drunk at the time of the incident.

The incident occurred on October 11 during an SFI march to Palakkad Town railway station in connection with a protest in Delhi. The marchers alleged that Mr. Safad, who arrived at the scene under the influence of alcohol, assaulted them using a knuckleduster.

A medical examination conducted at Government Taluk Hospital, Chittur, reportedly confirmed that the officer had consumed alcohol.

title: IIIT-Dharwad team secures fourth place in ISRO robotics challenge
text:
Team Icarus of the Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Dharwad, has secured fourth place in the ISRO Robotics Challenge–URSC (IRoC-U) 2026 and won a cash prize of ₹2 lakh.

The team comprised Jayesh Patil, Saksham Gupta, Aswin Joseph, Priyanshu Mittal, Raskin Verma, Ankit Dash and Mohammad Rehan.

Addressing a press conference at IIIT Dharwad on Tuesday, director S.R. Mahadeva Prasanna and Professor of Practice Mallikarjun Kande said the seven-member team was among 20 teams selected for the final round at the U.R. Rao Satellite Centre in Bengaluru after clearing the preliminary, qualification and elimination stages.

The team developed an autonomous heavy-payload quadcopter designed to operate in a simulated Mars-like environment without GPS connectivity. The drone could navigate autonomously, identify designated targets, execute mission operations and return to its base without human intervention.

Prof. Kande, who guided the team through the development and preparation phases, said that the system incorporated visual-inertial navigation, optical-flow-based navigation and computer vision for target detection. The students undertook extensive testing and debugging to integrate the hardware and software required for autonomous operations, he said.

The results were announced during the National Space Day celebrations and awards ceremony in Ahmedabad, organised with the involvement of the ISRO’s Space Applications Centre recently.

Prof. Prasanna said the achievement reflected the students’ technical expertise, perseverance, teamwork and innovation. It also demonstrated IIIT Dharwad students’ capabilities in autonomous robotics, aerial systems and technologies relevant to future space exploration, he said.

Professor K. Gopinath, in charge of student welfare, Registrar Satish Annigeri and the student achievers were present.

title: Terrorist hideout busted in J&K’s Poonch; AK-47, six hand grenades recovered
text:
A suspected terrorist hideout, inside a natural cave in the Surankote area of Poonch district in Jammu and Kashmir, was busted on Tuesday (October 13, 2026), leading to the recovery of an automatic rifle, six hand grenades and ammunition, officials said.

The arms cache was unearthed during a joint operation by the Army and the police at Satharban forest, following reports of suspicious movement in the area, officials said. An AK-47 rifle, a magazine, 30 rounds, six hand grenades and some medical supplies were recovered from the spot. No one was arrested during the operation.

In another development, officials said a search operation was under way in the higher reaches of Majalta and Billawar, spanning Udhampur and Kathua districts, following reports of suspicious movement.

The joint operation, involving Army personnel, including para commandos, and the police, has been under way since Monday (October 12, 2026) evening, in forest areas of Soan, Khuban, Chore and Nagan in Udhampur’s Majalta, and Sadrouta, Bhed and Balore in Kathua district. No contact had been established with the suspects so far, they added.

Separately, officials said Army troops detected two rusted landmines near the border fence in Basoni area of Mendhar sector in Poonch on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) morning. The landmines were spotted during ongoing track construction, they said, adding that both explosive devices were later destroyed by Army experts in a controlled explosion. More than a dozen landmines have been detected in the area and defused by the Army over the past week.

title: CEC-SIR issue: Rahul Gandhi's plea not listed for hearing in Supreme Court as defects yet to be cured
text:
The petition filed by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and 10 prominent opposition leaders following a massive march on October 12 was not listed for hearing in the Supreme Court on Tuesday (October 13) as defects pointed out by the registry are yet to be cured.

As per the Supreme Court's website, the apex court registry had flagged 14 defects, including lack of a clear copy of the ID card of Congress president and Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge, a co-petitioner in the case.

It has sought the constitution of an independent committee, headed by a retired apex court judge and assisted by technical experts and other citizens of eminence, to conduct a time-bound, independent audit of deletions and modifications made during the SIR.

title: Expelled leader Rahul Mamkootathil’s association with Congress workers exposes rift in Pathanamthitta unit
text:
Nearly a year after Rahul Mamkootathil was expelled from the Congress, his continued association with party workers has trigerred an infighting within the party in Pathanamthitta, with leaders at loggerheads over whether to stand by the former Palakkad MLA.

The latest flashpoint is the clash between Students’ Federation of India (SFI) and Youth Congress workers at Adoor General Hospital on Saturday night, in which Mr. Mamkootathil has been arraigned as an accused. Pathanamthitta District Congress Committee (DCC) president Satish Kochuparambil threw his weight behind the expelled leader in the aftermath, describing him as a Congress worker at heart. But the endorsement has drawn sharp objections from a section of district leaders and workers, who oppose any show of support for Mr. Mamkootathil, who had been expelled over allegations of sexual abuse of women.

Goes public

The simmering discontent spilled into the open on Tuesday, when Adoor Block Congress president Abid Shaheem publicly disowned Mr. Mamkootathil, making it clear that the former MLA could no longer claim to represent the party.

“Rahul Mamkootathil has a few friends here and they might have stood with him in that capacity. I was the State general secretary of the Youth Congress when he held the same position in the organisation. He later became the Youth Congress president and then a legislator. Following certain issues, he was expelled from the party after an inquiry,” Mr. Shaheem said.

He rejected any suggestion that the Congress in Adoor depended on Mr. Mamkootathil, pointing to its network of mandalam presidents, DCC office-bearers and booth presidents.

“If Mr. Mamkootathil is a member of the party, he can cooperate with it. But as long as he is not a member, he is not a Congress worker. If anyone comes to attack our party or workers, we will give them an appropriate response, whether physically or through legal means,” Mr. Shaheem said, adding that the Congress would protect Kerala Students’ Union (KSU) and Youth Congress workers.

The blunt remarks have left the district leadership on the back foot, with senior leaders appearing keen to avoid being drawn into the dispute. Mr. Kochuparambil, meanwhile, could not be reached for comment.

Rejects suggestion

Mr. Mamkootathil, for his part, took to social media to reject the suggestion that he wielded influence over either the Congress or the police in Adoor.

“The Congress in Adoor is controlled by the Adoor legislator and the KPCC, DCC and block-level leaders from Adoor. Not me. The police in Adoor listen to the SP, DySP, CI and other police personnel. Not me,” he wrote.

He also defended his decision to stand by party workers despite his expulsion, saying his commitment to them remained unchanged. “If my colleagues face any problem, I have clearly stated that I will stand with them, even at the cost of my life,” he added.

title: Russia's offensive ability is broken, Kyiv's former top general tells BBC
text:
Ukraine has stabilised the front line and "broken Russia's ability to advance" by killing so many of its men, Ukraine's former commander-in-chief has said in an interview with the BBC.

Gen Oleksandr Syrskyi made the comments in an exclusive interview, his first since he was dramatically forced from his post in the summer.

He addressed his sacking, disagreeing with his critics who declared him too "old school" to command Ukraine's new, technologically advanced forces.

He also pushed back against allegations made by soldiers who previously served under him, who told the BBC they were ordered to remain at their positions even when they were almost surrounded by Russians, leading to high losses.

Syrskyi said that Moscow's overall losses in the war were six times higher than Ukraine's. "If you count only dead, then it's up to 11 times," he added.

Neither Russia nor Ukraine officially release the numbers of their dead. Ukraine's military says it inflicted record losses this year on Russian soldiers in September, although that cannot be verified.

UK intelligence chiefs estimate Russia has lost around half a million men killed in Ukraine since launching its full-scale invasion in 2022. The US-based Center for Strategic and International Studies meanwhile believes, external Ukraine has lost up to 150,000 troops killed by June 2026.

He says this difference in death toll – as well as technological advances, and a strategy of attacking weak points in Russia's lines while containing their advances in other parts – accounts for the current stalemate at the front.

In the first six months of 2026, Russia managed overall to seize 61 sq km, the general said. "It's an indication that the front line has been stabilised."

The Institute for Study of War (ISW) has also confirmed this trend. One of its recent reports, external says that in September 2026, Moscow lost more territory than it took.

Syrskyi was appointed Ukraine's commander-in-chief in 2024. He had previously won praise for defending Kyiv at the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, and for leading the successful counteroffensive east of Kharkiv in the autumn of that year.

But President Volodymyr Zelensky fired Syrskyi this summer, amid a major disagreement with then-defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov.

Fedorov had said that instead of adapting to the realities of the changing war, the army under Syrskyi had blocked his initiatives.

Zelensky initially fired Fedorov, as tensions burst into the open between the two men. But mass street protests then forced the president to also fire Syrskyi, replacing him with Maj Gen Mykhailo Drapatyi, 43.

Syrskyi told the BBC that he had "disagreements" with Fedorov because the latter "didn't take into consideration the interests of the army" when procuring weapons and supplies.

title: Breaking Bad actor RJ Mitte dies aged 34
text:
US actor RJ Mitte, best known for his role as the defiant son of drug kingpin Walter White in the drama series Breaking Bad, has died at the age of 34.

"It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte," his representative told the BBC.

Mitte died in Brownsvillle, Texas, on Monday. His publicist confirmed that he took his own life.

The actor, who had cerebral palsy, drew on his own experience for his role as Walter 'Flynn' White Jr in the Emmy-winning drama series. Bryan Cranston, who played his father, led the tributes, writing that he was in "deep despair" following the news.

Cranston played a high school chemistry teacher who turned to a life of crime to support his family after a cancer diagnosis.

"I met him when he was only 14 years old when he was cast as Walter White Jr., a part he played with such joy and enthusiasm," said Cranston.

"That kid was pretty raw when we started shooting the pilot in February of 2007, but little by little we watched him grow into a really fine actor."

Cranston praised Mitte's advocacy for performers with disabilities, and noted that he never allowed his cerebral palsy to "be an excuse for anything".

"All that promise and potential now is such a loss," wrote the actor, adding that he "thoroughly enjoyed being with him throughout the years on the series, and after the spotlight on Breaking Bad dimmed".

He said "it is especially devastating to hear that he took his own life."

Cranston added: "I'll miss you, son."

Mitte's representative, Sean Reilly, said in a statement to the BBC: "Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion."

The star also served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children's.

He created The Mitte Foundation to support philanthropic efforts and community initiatives, using his platform "to challenge stereotypes and promote greater representation for people with disabilities", Reilly said.

In a statement shared with the Hollywood Reporter, Aaron Paul, who played Breaking Bad's Jesse Pinkman, said he was at a loss and heartbroken.

"RJ, I love you my friend. You will be missed," he said. "And to whoever happens to be reading this, please know you are loved, and you are not alone. Always remember that."

Dean Norris, who played Mitte's uncle, Hank Schrader, posted that although "RJ didn't play my TV son, I always looked out for him as a young kid on set".

"He was a sweetheart of a young man and will be greatly missed," Norris wrote.

Mitte, who grew up in Louisiana, was a young teen when he auditioned for the breakthrough role after moving to Los Angeles to support his younger sister's acting career in 2005.

He had said that his first audition in Los Angeles was for a California state public service announcement for an anti-meth commercial.

title: One dead and several hurt after rollercoaster incident at Six Flags
text:
One person has died and several others were injured after an incident on a rollercoaster at an amusement park in the state of Georgia.

The Cobb County Police Department said it was investigating the fatality at Six Flags Over Georgia, about 15 miles (24km) from Atlanta, according to the BBC's news partner CBS News.

Police did not specify which ride was involved, but aerial footage from news helicopters showed the Goliath rollercoaster stopped midway, with riders being helped off by workers.

Six Flags Over Georgia said it was "deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today. Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest's family, friends, and loved ones."

Officials have not said how the person died, or how the other riders were injured. The BBC has contacted local police and fire authorities, as well as park officials.

The identity of the person who died has also not been disclosed.

Witnesses told local media they saw a man ejected from the ride - an account of events that the BBC has not verified.

Local outlet 11 Alive quoted a witness saying the man had come loose from his seat, and had then struck the rollercoaster and some of his fellow riders before falling onto the roof of a nearby haunted house attraction.

The incident was captured in souvenir photos that were automatically taken of the rollercoaster while it was in motion, the witness added.

A husband and wife also told 11 Alive that the man had been ejected from the rollercoaster and had struck it afterwards. The couple said workers at the park had checked their safety harnesses before the ride set off.

title: Watch: Emergency calls from botched Christa Pike execution released
text:
A series of newly-released calls made after the failed execution of US death row inmate Christa Pike reveal emergency services were delayed by confusion among first responders and Tennessee prison officials.

The recordings, first obtained by the Associated Press, show that minutes passed as officials and responders attempted to confirm whether the request for emergency help in the execution chamber at Riverbend Prison was legitimate.

Pike, 50, was sentenced to death after murdering Colleen Slemmer with her then-boyfriend in 1995. She survived two injections of the drug pentobarbital on 30 September and was taken to hospital in a critical condition.

The BBC's Mayeni Jones explains.

title: Bulgaria summons Russian ambassador after ship sinks in Black Sea drone attack
text:
Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev has summoned the Russian ambassador after two merchant ships were struck by drones off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast.

Eleven crew members are missing and one sailor was saved, according to local officials, after one of the vessels sank 17 nautical miles (31km) east of the village of Krapets.

The other vessel, Ukrainian owned, was hit by drones 18 nautical miles from the town of Byala and all 15 crew were rescued.

The attacks come a week after two other commercial ships were hit by sea and aerial drones in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone. One of the ships, the Alfa Watan, sank and all 10 crew, including nine Syrians, are presumed dead.

Radev convened an emergency meeting on Tuesday and said he had summoned Russian envoy Eleonora Mitrofanova. Although there was no conclusive evidence of blame on "either side... the logic suggests that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation", he said.

Mitrofanova was later quoted by Bulgarian media as telling Radev she had no information from Russia's defence ministry relating to the latest attacks. She also said these strikes could have been a provocation by a third party.

Bulgaria is a Nato member, and Radev also spoke to secretary general Mark Rutte about the latest attacks.

"Nato will continue to work closely with our allies in the Black Sea," Rutte said after the talks.

"We have already strengthened our posture along the eastern flank and will continue to monitor the security environment, adjusting our deterrence and defence posture as needed," he added.

The two ships were struck just outside Bulgarian territorial waters.

If this had happened just a few nautical miles to the west, Article 5 of the Nato treaty could have been triggered. The article defines an armed attack on one member of the military alliance as an attack on all.

Radev had earlier asked Nato and the EU for technical assistance in investigating the previous attacks that took place on 6 October, indicating it was unclear who was behind them.

Radev came to office during the summer and has since rejected suggestions that he is "pro-Russian".

Ukraine has directly blamed Russia for the latest attacks and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen spoke on Tuesday of the Black Sea becoming "another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine. This is unacceptable".

Russia's military has not publicly commented on the issue. It has recently intensified its strikes on vessels in the Black Sea, particularly the western side, as part of its war against Ukraine.

The same day that two ships were targeted off Bulgaria last week, Ukraine hit an oil tanker in the Russian Black Sea port of Sochi.

Moscow says it is targeting ships delivering weapons and dual-use cargo to Ukrainian ports - and cited attacks in the ports of Mykolaiv and Chornomorsk last week, along with one in the Black Sea.

title: Hungarian MPs scrap Orbán's anti-LGBTQ measures
text:
The Hungarian parliament has voted to amend child protection laws, scrapping measures that stigmatise gay and transgender people. LGBTQ and human rights activists warmly welcomed the move, but called for changes to other Orbán-era laws.

The 2021 Child Protection Law, passed by the large Fidesz majority of then-Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, banned the "portrayal or promotion of homosexuality or transgenderism".

Since Orbán's April election defeat, the Tisza government of Péter Magyar has been working to dismantle the previous government's legacy.

Minutes after Tuesday's vote, Budapest said the EU had agreed to release €4.2bn (£3.5bn) of funds frozen in the last years of the Fidesz government.

The European Commission said last month that the Magyar government had addressed a number of "rule of law breaches affecting the EU budget", and urged EU leaders to unlock the funds , externaland readmit Hungary to two key EU programmes - Erasmus+ and Horizon Europe.

Hungary's 2021 law had affected a wide range of other laws, including education and the right of assembly.

Magyar's Tisza party commands the same two-thirds majority that Orbán's party used to have, and the measures passed on Tuesday were bundled together by the new government in a package of laws designed to unravel the Fidesz legislation.

"We are very happy that this got adopted," Tamás Dombos of civil rights group the Háttér Society told the BBC. "We've been fighting this so-called child protection law for five years. There have been problems with the bill submitted to parliament, but most of those problems have been fixed."

Both the Fidesz and Tisza governments made child protection central to their image.

But while Fidesz under Viktor Orbán appealed to the conservative electorate by identifying gay and transgender people as a threat to public morals, Tisza under Prime Minister Péter Magyar is trying to remove or soften legislation, without actually identifying as a liberal-minded government in favour of full equality.

In June 2025, the Gay Pride march through Budapest drew an estimated quarter of a million people, despite a promise by then-Prime Minister Viktor Orbán to his supporters that he would prevent it happening.

Police stood aside despite an official ban, and proceedings against the city mayor and others for organising the festival were later dropped. This year's event went ahead without restrictions.

The child protection issue turned from being a strong card in Orbán's hand to become his Achilles heel, when the public found out that his government had supported the pardon of the deputy head of a children's home who had been found guilty of covering up the paedophile crimes of his boss.

In his own election campaign, Péter Magyar presented his party as a champion of the rights of children in state care, while painstakingly avoiding the issues of gay and transgender rights, for fear of alienating right-wing voters.

title: Super El Niño sets another record as it strengthens to 'unprecedented levels'
text:
El Niño has continued to strengthen to what some scientists are calling "unprecedented levels", weeks before its expected peak in December.

Several key measures are now in record territory.

In its latest update, Australia's Bureau of Meteorology (BOM) said average weekly sea-surface temperatures in the central Pacific have reached their highest level on record, external.

It comes after scientists declared a new record for daily sea surface temperatures in the central-eastern Pacific in September, exceeding the previous record set during the very strong El Niño of 2015.

Temperatures above 30C have also been recorded for the first time in parts of the tropical Pacific, while record sea-surface temperature anomalies and exceptional subsurface warmth have been observed.

These measurements come from the region of the equatorial Pacific used to monitor El Niño.

El Niño is a naturally-occurring pattern, which happens about every two to seven years and tends to last for around a year.

However, the Pacific is also warming due to human-induced climate change and this is starting to mask the strength of the natural warming during El Niño.

To remove this additional warming signal, Australian and US official forecasters are now using a Relative Ocean El Niño Index (RONI), to enable better comparison to historical events.

Using that measure, the BOM's average weekly data - while only going back to 2008 - is significant as it now exceeds levels during the record-breaking December of 2015.

"We are currently witnessing an El Niño event that is unprecedented in the historical record," Dr Zeke Hausfather, a climate scientist at Berkeley Earth, told the BBC.

The warmth across the Pacific now extends well beyond the tropical region normally used to monitor El Niño.

Comparisons with previous major events in 1972-73, 1982-83, 1997-98 and 2015-16 show much more widespread ocean warmth across the Pacific and into the Gulf of Mexico.

Part of this reflects the long-term warming of the oceans but scientists say it is not the whole story.

"The strength of El Niño this year is spilling out of the traditional El Niño region," Dr Hausfather said.

The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) says there is currently no evidence that climate change is making El Niño events stronger or more frequent, external. However, it remains an active area of scientific research.

What is clearer is that El Niño releases additional heat from the oceans into the atmosphere.

Historically, global temperatures during El Niño years are typically higher than during neutral years.

Combined with human-driven climate change, that extra heat is expected to help make 2026 one of the warmest years on record, with unusually high global temperatures likely to continue into 2027.

Although the most widespread impacts are expected later this year and into 2027, El Niño's influence is already being felt across parts of the world.

title: Ex-president named leader of new DR Congo rebel coalition
text:
Former Congolese President Joseph Kabila has been named the leader of a new rebel coalition seeking to oust the government.

The Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN) said it aimed to coordinate "resistance forces" to end "tyranny" in Democratic Republic of Congo and would pursue the goal "by all means, including force".

Its unveiling on Monday is the clearest indication so far of Kabila's direct involvement in an armed movement a year after he was sentenced to death in absentia for treason. He had previously denied having links to the M23 rebel group.

The Congolese government has not commented.

Claude Ibalanky, the coalition's adviser, announced the group's leadership at a press conference at Kabila's residence in Goma, the largest city in eastern DR Congo, which has been under the control of the M23 since last year.

Video released by the group showed Kabila signing documents at the group's declaration along with other leaders.

M23 leader Sultani Makenga will serve as one of Kabila's four deputies in the new movement. The other three also come from the AFC-M23 alliance which last year seized much of mineral-rich eastern DR Congo.

The announcement of the new group comes days after Kabila delivered an address in which he said he would set out how Congolese people should act to "rescue" their country.

On Friday, Kabila accused President Félix Tshisekedi's government of disregarding proposals he had put forward last year, including some aimed at ending the conflict in eastern DR Congo.

Kabila also accused the government of undermining constitutional rule, mismanaging the economy and failing to improve security. He further alleged arbitrary arrests of political opponents and military officers.

The government has not publicly responded to those claims.

Kabila, 55, ruled DR Congo from 2001 until January 2019, when Tshisekedi took office following a disputed election.

The two were once political allies, forming an informal power-sharing arrangement after the transfer of power. They later fell out and Kabila went into self-imposed exile in 2023 before returning to Goma last year.

The former president had remained largely out of public view for several years but has become increasingly critical of his successor's administration.

The formation of the new coalition comes at an uncertain time in a country that has been wracked by violence for decades.

More than 100 militia groups are active in eastern DR Congo amid ethnic tensions and fighting for political power and control of lucrative natural resources.

The UN and Western governments accuse Rwanda of backing the M23 and controlling the rebels.

Rwanda denies supporting the M23 despite overwhelming evidence, and says its military presence in eastern DR Congo is a defensive measure against threats posed by Congolese armed groups.

Tshisekedi's second term ends in 2028 but in May he said that elections, which are due then, may not be held because of the conflict.

title: Six Ukrainian energy sites hit by Russia since Trump announced ceasefire, Zelensky says
text:
Russia struck six Ukrainian energy facilities hours after US President Donald Trump announced the two countries had agreed to an energy ceasefire, Volodymyr Zelensky has said.

Despite Trump stating on Sunday the truce would be "effective immediately", the Ukrainian president said Russia had hit "our gas stations, energy infrastructure, and other facilities".

There were blackouts in the city of Izyum after a Russian strike destroyed power grids, Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform said, while energy and railway infrastructure in western Ukraine was also targeted overnight.

On Monday, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Ukraine does not deserve the "respite" a ceasefire would bring.

Zelensky said 33 people had been injured in the strikes on energy facilities across the country.

He told Fox News: "We did not attack, while Russia attacked our gas stations, energy infrastructure, and other facilities."

"I think it was Putin's answer to President Trump," he added.

Global conflicts have pushed fuel prices higher ahead of the US midterm elections and on Friday Trump announced a plan to import Russian diesel into the US on Friday.

On Monday, Ukraine's state-owned grid operator Ukrenergo reported "new power cuts" in Kharkiv, Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia due to damage caused to energy equipment by Russian attacks.

Electricity rationing has been introduced in parts of Ukraine to avoid overloading damaged equipment, Ukrenergo said.

Zelensky said on X the strikes were proof Russia was "unwilling to accept an energy ceasefire".

On Monday evening, Kyiv's mayor Vitali Klitschko posted on Telegram that a drone hit a 25-story residential building in the Darnytskyi district.

Several cars in the building's courtyard were also on fire, he said, with one person dead and 11 injured.

When Trump first announced the ceasefire on Sunday, Zelensky said it was "news to him" that a truce was in effect, but he backed the proposed ceasefire as a "major step toward ending the war, if the Americans truly step in now and make sure Russians respect the energy ceasefire".

Asked about the ceasefire on Monday, Trump said they agreed "because I said you agree", adding that the war "has to get settled".

"That war is a disaster if you see the numbers," he said.

For months, Ukraine and Russia have been exchanging strikes on energy infrastructure, disrupting energy supplies on both sides.

Moscow has said the installations it hits are legitimate targets as they support Ukraine's military operation, while Zelensky has characterised Ukrainian attacks deep inside Russian territory as part of an effort to "reduce Russia's ability to finance the war".

Analysis by BBC Verify on both Ukrainian and Russian strikes during the war have found both sides have increased their attacks in the lead up to the next winter.

title: India 'cockroach' leaders detained after entering barricaded protest site
text:
Leaders of India's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) were detained early on Tuesday after they entered a heavily-guarded protest site and chanted slogans demanding the country's election chief resign over a controversial revision of electoral rolls.

Party founder Abhijeet Dipke shared a video showing Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das being taken away by police from Jantar Mantar, a historic Delhi observatory popular for protests.

Footage showed the two - along with others - climbing over police barricades before chanting slogans while holding the Indian flag.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi's opponents allege the voter list revision benefits his party, a charge it and the Election Commission reject.

There have been days of protests demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.

Police have stepped up security across Delhi as demonstrators challenge restrictions on where protests can be held.

Early on Tuesday, Dipke, Das and Ranka all shared videos showing Das and Ranka entering Jantar Mantar.

"You cannot denotify the resistance," Dipke wrote on X.

Das also posted a message declaring that the site had been "reclaimed" and that they were being detained.

It was not immediately clear where police had taken the leaders.

Ranka later appeared on an Instagram live broadcast from a police bus alongside other detainees where they appeared cheerful and said they would not back down.

The detentions came a day after the federal home ministry announced that Jantar Mantar, long associated with public protests in Delhi, would no longer be a designated protest venue. Authorities instead identified three alternative locations where demonstrations can be held with permission.

Before the decision, the CJP had met Delhi Police officials to seek permission for a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar and had warned that it would announce further demonstrations if it received no response.

"30 mins after we went to Delhi Police asking for a date when we can go to Jantar Mantar, Jantar Mantar was de-notified as a protest site," Ranka had earlier posted on X.

Most of the party's leadership has been in Delhi in recent days. Dipke, however, had travelled to his hometown in Maharashtra after the death of his grandmother. He was among several CJP leaders detained ahead of a planned demonstration on Saturday and was released the next day.

The CJP had called for a protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, but authorities imposed extensive security restrictions across the capital to prevent demonstrators from reaching the site.

Several metro stations were closed, train services were disrupted and thousands of police and paramilitary personnel were deployed.

Over the weekend, the police detained and released thousands of people, including several journalists. Some videos and photos from the protest show police dragging people, including women, by force and pushing them into buses.

title: Watch: US man eyes pumpkin world record after fifth contest win
text:
A five-time US giant pumpkin contest winner tells the BBC he'd "love" to break the world record for a second time.

Horticulture teacher Travis Gienger hauled his pumpkin from Minnesota to Half Moon Bay, California, for the annual pumpkin weighing event.

His whopping gourd took home the prize, tipping the scales at 2,389 pounds (1,083kg).

But Gienger says he's eyeing off a different prize – the world record title – which was set in England's south coast last week with a squash weighing in at 2,857 pounds (1,300kg).

As a previous holder of the world-record mantle, Gienger says he's focused on the challenge ahead.

title: South Africa's deputy police chief resigns after being charged with sexual offences
text:
South Africa's deputy police chief has resigned three weeks after he was charged with sexual offences.

A lawyer representing Lt Gen Shadrack Sibiya submitted his resignation letter at his disciplinary hearing on Monday, a police spokesperson said.

Sibiya, 59, is also accused of having links to organised crime bosses - allegations which led to him being suspended last year.

He denies those allegations, as well as charges that he sexually groomed a 16-year-old girl and raped an 18-year-old woman. He also faces a charge of human trafficking.

Sibiya says he did have sex with the 18-year-old but that it was consensual.

He has been in custody since he was arrested three weeks ago.

Police spokesperson Athlenda Mathe said in a post on X that his departure from the police force was regarded as a dishonourable discharge, external because he was still facing a disciplinary case when he resigned.

The accusations that Sibiya was linked to crime bosses emerged at a major public inquiry over allegations of police corruption and collusion with criminals, known as the Madlanga Commission.

Sibiya was accused of interfering with investigations into political killings in KwaZulu-Natal province.

He was also accused of receiving a gift of cash, as well as 20 impalas, from an alleged criminal kingpin in exchange for a police contract.

He denied the allegation.

The Madlanga Commission has transfixed South Africa over the past year and unearthed widespread allegations of links between police officers and crime bosses.

It was set up by President Cyril Ramaphosa after the KwaZulu-Natal police chief held a press briefing where he accused the then Police Minister Senzo Mchunu of working with criminal gangs.

Mchunu denies the allegations against him but has been suspended.

title: Documents falsified to evade tax on Abramovich's wealth, BBC finds
text:
The world's biggest accountancy firm helped in falsifying documents to hide Roman Abramovich's wealth and evade tax, BBC Panorama has found.

Accounts signed off by Deloitte in Cyprus meant assets such as superyachts, mansions and private jets worth $672m (£508m) vanished from Abramovich's company accounts.

Deloitte also appears to have advised on a scheme to evade a huge tax bill on the oligarch's wealth through the falsification of documents.

Barrister Andrew Mitchell KC, an expert in financial services law, said Panorama's evidence showed the scheme was "straightforward" tax evasion and "it couldn't be more blatant".

Roman Abramovich's lawyers said he denies that he evaded tax or concealed his fortune. They said Panorama provided no evidence he knew about, authorised or directed the falsification of any document and said it was legitimate to rely on advice from professionals.

Deloitte Cyprus said it "acts in compliance with applicable laws".

The findings are being revealed following a joint investigation between BBC Panorama and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism.

For nearly two decades, Roman Abramovich was the most famous Russian oligarch in the UK, welcomed in London where he bought Chelsea Football Club in 2003 and bankrolled the club's most successful period. But after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, he was sanctioned by the UK government as an associate of President Vladimir Putin and forced to sell the club.

Abramovich has been reported to be living in Turkey, a safe haven for him because it did not apply sanctions. In the Channel Island of Jersey, £5.4bn of his assets remain frozen and a criminal investigation has been going on for four years.

The oligarch's lawyers told the BBC he denies the allegations in the Jersey investigation and says it was "undertaken for political purposes".

Our investigation has uncovered new evidence about the way Abramovich's business empire has been run. It also raises serious questions about the integrity of some of his professional advisers.

The evidence is contained in a leak that includes thousands of documents about the oligarch's finances and the operations of a network of offshore companies administered from Cyprus - which used to be a tax haven popular with Russians - between 1995 and 2022.

The BBC and media partners including the Guardian, Paper Trail Media, the Organised Crime and Corruption Reporting Project, and the Cyprus Investigative Reporting Network - as well as the Bureau of Investigative Journalism, external - have been reporting on the leaked files since 2023 as part of the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists' Cyprus Confidential, external investigation.

title: Immigration agents search congresswoman Ilhan Omar's home
text:
US immigration agents have searched the home of Minnesota Representative Ilhan Omar as part of a criminal investigation.

Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agents "executed a judicially authorised search warrant" for the property in the Washington DC area, a US justice department spokesperson said.

The search "is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation", the spokesperson said, but no further details were given. The US Congress is currently out of session and it is unclear if Omar was at the home.

Omar, a Democrat and outspoken critic of President Donald Trump, described the search on social media as "an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement".

"For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns," Omar said in the post.

"This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced."

Speaking to reporters on Monday, Trump said he had "nothing to do" with the justice department's investigation into Omar, while describing her as a "complainer" and a "terrible person".

The Republican president said of the Somali-born congresswoman: "She comes from a country that is a non-country.

"And then she comes over here and she complains about our Constitution."

At a rally in Ohio later on Monday, Trump referred to the search of Omar's home, saying: "I don't know what they're doing with it, but I can tell you this: she's a disaster."

Trump went on to denigrate Somalis in the US more generally, which was greeted with chants of "deport" in the crowd, US media reported.

Omar's communications director, Jacklyn Rogers, called Monday morning's raid "an outrageous abuse of power" by the Trump administration, and said the congresswoman "has done nothing wrong".

The nature of the criminal investigation remains unclear.

An ally of Omar gave an update to the BBC World Service's Newsday programme. Asma Mohammed said: "She is doing well, she's let everyone know that she's okay and that she is used to attacks from the president but this is a new low from him."

During Monday's search, a BBC crew saw several agents at Omar's home, some carrying boxes to a van.

News of the search was first reported by Fox News, which said the investigation was about immigration paperwork filed by her late father when Omar was a child.

The timing of the raid - 22 days before the November midterm elections, which will decide the balance of power in Congress for the next two years - raised concerns from Omar's fellow Democrats.

The justice department has a longstanding policy of refraining from most enforcement action that is "likely to raise an issue or the perception" it is being brought for the purpose of affecting any election or to disadvantage a candidate.

Leading Democrats in the House of Representatives said in a statement that Omar had long been targeted with "vile personal attacks and baseless accusations" by Trump.

title: Is Zelensky right to say data centre strikes have taken down Russian bots?
text:
Claims that Ukrainian strikes on Russian data centres reduced Kremlin-linked bot networks have spread widely online, but experts have told BBC Verify there is no evidence the attacks have significantly reduced them.

Viral social media posts have claimed there has been a significant drop in influence operations in recent days, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky suggesting on Monday there was "less hate, less division and fewer provocations" online because of "fewer bots".

Russian influence operations, which promote pro-Kremlin narratives and spread disinformation, have been tracked by researchers and journalists including BBC Verify for more than a decade.

These campaigns push disinformation on to people's social media feeds on issues like the Ukraine war or post messages in support of Moscow's interests.

Ukraine has struck three of Russian tech giant Yandex's five data centres since 8 October in response to Moscow's attacks on Ukrainian internet hubs.

The second of these strikes on Thursday caused Yandex, often referred to as Russia's Google, to announce it was struggling to maintain its services.

But claims these attacks have affected Russian disinformation operations, including accounts posting supportive messages about groups including the Make American Great Again (MAGA) movement in the US and the far-right AfD party in Germany, appear to have come from a misinterpretation of data produced by tech firm Cloudflare.

Some social media users have been sharing charts of Cloudflare data which show bot activity using Yandex's network has declined.

While bots are commonly associated with fake social media accounts that may post false, divisive and inflammatory content, they are also used to automate tasks like scanning web pages so they appear on search engines.

title: The island where locals say data centres are taking their water
text:
"Water! Water!" the crowd shouted as it stormed a compound with data centres, armed with empty plastic bottles and jerry cans.

There were about 300 of them, all residents on the Indonesian island of Batam, and they were furious that the taps at home had run dry, while the data centres in the new Nongsa Digital Park seemed to have enough water to protect their machines from overheating.

"Not a single drop has come through our taps for the last three months... Our water supply had been reliable until the data centres came," Dewi Susanti, one of the protesters, told the BBC.

People in her village, Bakau Serip, were now depending on tanker trucks that dispensed "dirty, cloudy and smelly" water, she said.

Batam's water utility told the BBC it was working to improve supply, but did not comment on whether the disruption was linked to demand from the data centres.

But BP Batam, the agency overseeing trade and industry, blamed it on a prolonged dry spell and denied allegations from locals that water meant for homes was being channelled to data centres.

This is not the first such protest in Batam, whose shrinking reservoirs find themselves under more pressure as the island tries to transform itself into a digital hub.

Following protests in August and September, authorities told the firms opening data centres in Batam that they must build their own desalination plants instead of relying on reservoirs for freshwater.

But locals say they are increasingly concerned that they must now compete with servers for water.

"Reliable data on data centre water use in Indonesia remains scarce, partly because companies treat it as proprietary information," says Agus Hasan, a professor at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology.

"We should build [data centres] rationally, transparently, and responsibly, and insist on seeing the numbers... [Otherwise] those kept in the dark while their taps run dry will push back, and rightly so," he adds.

A backlash has been building against data centres across the world, from the US to the UK to parts of Asia, as tech companies pour billions into AI infrastructure.

People are worried about how the huge, windowless buildings might change their neighbourhoods, the constant hum of machines, the security lights that could stay on all night, and the pressure this puts on water and energy resources.

While electricity powers the centres, the water keeps the servers from frying – engineers deploy elaborate cooling systems, which consume a lot of water.

Research in the US suggests a typical data centre consumes around 300,000 gallons of water a day, or about as much as 1,000 US households. title: Boardroom feud tests trusted Indian business empire
text:
Before dawn breaks over Mumbai, Mansi Kadam begins preparing vada pav, a savoury snack synonymous with the western Indian city, for the day's customers. One ingredient is non-negotiable: Tata salt.

When asked whether she would ever consider switching brands, her reply is a reminder of an old Hindi ad jingle, "If it's salt, it has to be Tata."

She knows little about the developments unfolding in the boardroom of the Tata group, one of India's oldest and most influential business empires that makes everything from salt to software.

But her instinctive loyalty points to a question confronting the group: Can one of India's most trusted brands remain insulated from a public battle over power, governance and control?

A recent public disagreement between the board of Tata Sons, the holding company of the Tata group and Tata Trusts, its principal shareholder, has put a spotlight on the conglomerate.

At the centre of the dispute are two issues - the proposed public listing of Tata Sons and the reappointment of chairman N Chandrasekaran. Most of the Tata Sons board, including its biggest minority shareholder SP Group, supported the decisions.

But Noel Tata, chairman of majority shareholder Tata Trusts, has opposed both resolutions. He maintains that a public listing would dilute the group's philanthropic ethos and is likely to get both decisions overturned at its annual general meeting.

"When we say this is a governance crisis, it's a misalignment of interests between the board [of Tata Sons] and the shareholders [Tata Trusts]," Shriram Subramanian, head of independent corporate governance firm InGovern Research, told the BBC.

While he does not expect the brand's image to be affected immediately, he flags concerns over the leadership's ability to navigate the challenges.

Disagreements within the Tata Group have been simmering since the death of former chairman Ratan Tata - Noel Tata's half-brother who designated him successor after his death - in 2024. For many Indians, Ratan Tata's philanthropy and leadership had become inseparable from the brand. His death triggered widespread mourning and experts say it left a leadership void in the group's image with the public.

The Tata group has topped India's most valuable brand list by valuation consultancy Brand Finance since 2018, according to the group's website.

Tata Sons, the business entity, is described by the group as the "fastener keeping the many disparate elements of the whole together".

Tata Trusts, which represents seven philanthropic trusts that own the majority stake in the group, is widely regarded as its moral compass, guiding the businesses on social impact and philanthropy.

For many Indians, both the entities together make up what most companies cannot buy - trust.

Now with these entities in rival corners, that is coming under strain.

title: Death threats and isolation - the cost of fighting sexual violence in Iraq
text:
